{{short description|South African tennis player}} {{BLP sources|date=November 2010}} {{Use South African English|date=May 2013}} {{Use dmy dates|date=June 2021}} {{Infobox tennis biography | name = Mariaan de Swardt | image = | country = {{RSA}} | residence = [[Houston, Texas]], U.S. | birth_date = {{Birth date and age|df=yes|1971|03|18}} | birth_place = [[Johannesburg]], South Africa | height = 1.77 m | turnedpro = 1988 | retired = 2001 | plays = Right (one handed-backhand) | careerprizemoney = $1,127,365 | singlesrecord = {{tennis record|won=204|lost=136}} | singlestitles = 1 | highestsinglesranking = No. 28 (8 April 1996) | AustralianOpenresult = 1R (1995, 1996, 1999) | FrenchOpenresult = 3R (1999) | Wimbledonresult = 4R (1995) | USOpenresult = 3R (1994) | doublesrecord = {{tennis record|won=196|lost=131}} | doublestitles = 4 | highestdoublesranking = No. 11 (19 October 1998) | AustralianOpenDoublesresult = 3R (1996, 1999) | FrenchOpenDoublesresult = QF (1996) | WimbledonDoublesresult = F (1999) | USOpenDoublesresult = QF (1996) | AustralianOpenMixedresult = '''W''' (1999) | FrenchOpenMixedresult = '''W''' (2000) }} '''Mariaan de Swardt''' (born 18 March 1971) is a former professional tennis player from South Africa, who was active from 1988 to 2001. She twice represented her native country at the [[Summer Olympics]], in [[Tennis at the 1992 Summer Olympics|1992]] and [[Tennis at the 1996 Summer Olympics|1996]],{{cite Sports-Reference |url=https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/de/mariaan-de-swardt-1.html |title=Mariaan de Swardt |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200418062156/https://www.sports-reference.com/olympics/athletes/de/mariaan-de-swardt-1.html |archive-date=2020-04-18}} and was a member of the [[South Africa Fed Cup team]] in 1992 and from 1994 to 1997. In 2006, de Swardt became a U.S. citizen.{{Citation needed|date=November 2010}} De Swardt won two Grand Slam titles in mixed-doubles competition, the [[1999 Australian Open]] and the [[2000 French Open]] with partner [[David Adams (tennis)|David Adams]].{{cite web|title=Kafelnikov captures Open title|url=https://news.bbc.co.uk/1/hi/world/africa/268571.stm|website=BBC News|date=31 January 1999}}{{cite book|last1=Djata|first1=Sundiata|title=Blacks at the Net : Black Achievement in the History of Tennis.|date=2008|publisher=Syracuse University Press|location=Syracuse, N.Y.|isbn=978-0815608981|page=82|edition=1}} She also won four women's doubles titles and reached as high as world No. 11 in the doubles [[WTA rankings]]. She has one [[WTA Tour]] singles title from 1998 and reached a career-high singles ranking of world No. 28 in 1996. Since retiring from tennis, she has been a commentator for [[Eurosport]] and South African television, and has coached at professional, collegiate and recreational level with her base being at Atlanta, Georgia. She resides in Houston, Texas, and is a teaching professional at The Houstonian Club. In 2004, she set up a non-profit charity, the Pet Care Fund, to help animals.{{cite web|url=http://www.middlestates.usta.com/Events---New/20234_Mariaan_de_Swardt/|title=Mariaan de Swardt Biography|access-date=2011-11-09|archive-date=2 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120402095442/http://www.middlestates.usta.com/Events---New/20234_Mariaan_de_Swardt/|url-status=dead}} ==Grand Slam tournament finals== ===Doubles: 1 (runner-up)=== {|class="sortable wikitable" !Result !Year !style="width:110px"|Championship !style="width:50px"|Surface !style="width:150px"|Partner !style="width:150px"|Opponents !style="width:100px" class="unsortable"|Score |- " | style="background:#ffa07a;"|Loss | 1999 | style="background:#ccffcc;"|[[Wimbledon Championships|Wimbledon]] | Grass | {{flagicon|UKR}} [[Elena Tatarkova]] | {{flagicon|USA}} [[Lindsay Davenport]]
